decisions.reason: Report cites fixture/plugin-dock-chips.js and quotes the exact disabled expression in AttachmentChips, explains busy is AttachButton's local state unbound in AttachmentChips/module scope, and shows empty occurrences return null before the map while a plain-phase present occurrence makes the left guard false so busy evaluates and throws ReferenceError. Table reproduces the short-circuit truth behavior; source grounding is satisfied by the named file and unambiguous component/line.

Section 1.4 explains the slot-level React error boundary catches the render exception and unmounts the entire slot entry (whole dock tree, not just the remove button), that the attach button survives as a separate input.left slot entry, and that the error appears only in the browser console with no user-facing banner.

Uses shipped v0.2.10 source plus the maintainer note to establish busy predates v0.2.11, treats the diff's old-side hunk as an artifact, and proposes both a rollback/re-add bisect and a minimal data-present plain-phase mount on v0.2.10 code with a distinguishing-evidence table (stack location, invariance to reverting the diff). It does not claim the diff is harmless: it flags the diff as inconsistent with the baseline on the old disabled line and identifies the imageItem line referencing status/record before the map callback declares them, crediting these extra defects. It also explicitly notes historical usage frequency is inferred rather than proven.

Fix removes the dangling busy reference (or lifts shared/pending state as a properly owned prop) while preserving the phase guard; hardening adds record?.items ?? [] before .find (explaining the TypeError on a record without items) and event.target.closest?.() with rationale; the imageItem lookup is moved inside the map callback where record/status are scoped. Equivalent safe fixes, no execution required.

Proposes a jsdom render smoke of AttachmentDock with a matching occurrence in plain phase asserting .chip and .remove exist and no error-boundary/console.error capture, and explains why the empty state passes vacuously through return null and why node --check/syntax gates cannot catch free identifiers (legal parse, runtime-only failure). Includes the data-present render smoke as a minimum pre-ship check for slot-rendering lib-only plugins; no actual test run demanded.
